MELEE PC PORT - CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (2026-10-14)
Status: development diagnostics; not a playable release. PORT_PROGRESS.txt records historical evidence; its early baseline statements are historical, not current capability claims.

WIDESCREEN MENU/FMV REGRESSION CHECK (2026-10-14): `work/verify-widescreen-compositor-captures.py` independently validates all six saved title-menu/opening-FMV compositor artifacts at 16:9, 16:10, and 21:9. It checks image dimensions, centered symmetric pure-black side bars, a 4:3 content viewport, and artifact integrity; it is deliberately explicit that the output-sized compositor twin is not direct OS scanout. Expected verified viewports are 720x540 with 120px side bars at 960x540, 800x600 with 80px side bars at 960x600, and 720x540 with 270px side bars at 1260x540. Re-run this oracle after compositor/aspect changes. This is an artifact regression gate, not a substitute for direct display QA, additional menu/FMV scenes, or stable transition coverage.

NATIVE IN-GAME SETTINGS REQUIREMENT (2026-10-14): All graphics and audio controls must live in native game-owned menu pages, not Aurora's separate host/window options dock. Roadmap pages: Display (16:9/16:10/21:9, render resolution 240p–8K, Auto/D3D11/D3D12/Vulkan capability-aware renderer choice, and 120/240 Hz presentation only after decoupled pacing acceptance); Graphics (FSR3 when supported, shadow resolution, texture quality); Advanced Graphics (shadows on/off, textures at 100/50/25%, lighting on/off, force lowest available model LOD without changing collision/gameplay). Audio offers stereo and actual 5.1 with device checks and safe stereo fallback. Keep settings session-only unless persistence is explicitly approved. Each control must show its effective value, respect capability limits, and be verified by changing it from the native menu and observing runtime/readback effects. Source/runtime evidence exists for texture-quality, lighting, fighter-shadow enable/resolution, and low-detail fighter model selection. Current Settings → Display evidence supersedes the older v223-v225 navigation failures: muted D3D12 v350 synthetic virtual-pad runs reached the native Graphics page, visited all seven rows, matched requested setting readbacks, and returned with Back to parent Settings. Composited captures cover 4:3 (640x480), 16:9 (960x540), 16:10 (960x600), and 21:9 (1260x540). Evidence: work/native-graphics-menu-v350-visual-verification.json and work/native-graphics-menu-v350-aspect-contact.png; D3D12 v350 workspace diagnostic candidate SHA-256 334CD050FCB138B8C7FE24E095364B96D91CAA49702F4E7750E1C011D8D748B1 (not the current Desktop native-preview/melee.exe, whose D3D11 SHA-256 is 6EFD13A82878CD563FD19D408A037026DC39E8DA00553352573732B3F8EAF938). This verifies menu routing/readbacks on one D3D12 host with synthetic input only; physical input, direct scanout, long sessions, other renderers, and release acceptance remain open. Renderer selection is now wired into this page using Auto and compiled D3D11/D3D12/Vulkan candidates, with a child-process restart/apply handoff; in-game visual/input behavior and device-specific backend switching are still unverified. 120/240 Hz controls, FSR3, and broader device-capability feedback remain pending. Keep the settings feature incomplete until these broader gates pass.

RENDERING AND SETTINGS
FRAME-PACING INTEGRATION GATE (2026-10-12): frame_clock.c/h and the 60/120/240 arithmetic unit test exist, but production contains no call to MeleePc_FrameClockInit/Advance. The scene owner loop consumes the PAD sample queue (sample period capped at 60 Hz), runs scene/GObj update callbacks, then invokes GX render callbacks, copies XFB, and ends one Aurora frame in the same iteration. This is not independent 120/240 Hz presentation. Next design and integrate a real owner-thread scheduler that preserves 60 Hz simulation/input edge semantics and can present at target refresh without rerunning gameplay callbacks; account for XFB availability, pause, catch-up, queue backpressure, and orderly shutdown. Measure actual presented frames and simulation ticks at 60/120/240 on both backends; unit arithmetic, vsync capability selection, or duplicated 60 Hz frames alone do not meet acceptance. Audit: native-frame-pacing-integration-audit.json.
Auto/D3D11/D3D12/Vulkan renderer capability checks and main-menu selection. Prefer D3D12 if measured better; retain Vulkan compatibility. Vulkan now has bounded original-menu/CSS/Battlefield match and private active-frame visual evidence (Bowser/Pikachu, HUD, timer); stage defects remain. Full-match stability, timing and compatibility on other machines remain unverified.
LOW-END SETTING / HIGH-REFRESH PROBE (2026-10-15): A bounded muted D3D12 Yoshi's Story match ran the full repeat-deadline GX redraw path with 240p accepted, lighting disabled, and low-poly fighters requested. Analyzer verified 20 pacing windows: median presentation 87.82 Hz (range 61.18–112.56), while simulation median was 47.71 Hz (31.09–59.53). This is a full-render-callback attempt, not an XFB-only repeat; it still misses 120 Hz and stable 60 Hz gameplay. It does not prove every output image differed or add interpolation between game states. The low-poly setter was requested successfully (startup would abort on failure) but has no explicit readback marker. Evidence: `work/yoshi-fox-sudden-death-repeat-render-120-low-settings-600-d3d12-trace-analysis.json` and the matching trace/capture. Do not repeat this exact profile. Next optimize actual owner-loop/XFB/render cost and integrate a fixed-step scheduler with input/back-pressure tests before adding a user-facing refresh option. No product-source change, saves touched, or disc modified; overall estimate remains 25%.
SIMULATION-FIRST HIGH-REFRESH DIAGNOSTIC IMPROVEMENT (2026-10-15): The opt-in `MELEE_DIAGNOSTIC_REPEAT_RENDER_HZ` path in `src/melee/gm/gmscene.c` no longer inserts extra full redraws between queued 60Hz input/simulation samples by default. The previous behavior is still available only with the explicit `MELEE_DIAGNOSTIC_REPEAT_RENDER_DURING_BACKLOG` flag. Rebuilt the Release Melee library and linked a separate x86 D3D12 diagnostic host. Under the same bounded 240p/light-off/low-poly Yoshi/Fox probe, measured simulation median improved from 47.71 to 59.54 Hz; presentation median remained 86.43 Hz and did not reach 120. Minimum simulation window was 38.73 Hz, so stable 60Hz is not yet proven. This is a diagnostic owner-loop guard, not a user-facing setting, interpolation, unique-output-image proof, or acceptance. Evidence: `work/native-high-refresh-simulation-priority-comparison-20261015.json`. Normal gameplay code paths remain unchanged unless the diagnostic repeat-rate flag is used. Overall estimate remains 25%.

TWO BUNDLED TARGETS
Local Windows executable: native single-player plus four-player P2P lobbies.
Separate browser-host executable/build: configurable IP/hostname and port join URL, genuine client-side browser game runtime with rendering/input/audio/networking, authorized asset transfer, integrity checks, per-client download progress and readiness in lobby. Validate secure browser context and network reachability. A web page or streamed desktop does not prove browser-native play.
Technical asset transfer does not grant redistribution rights. Serve only assets the host is authorized to distribute.
Browser hardware compatibility requirement: treat older x86 CPUs and ARM64 devices such as compatible Chromebooks as explicit targets for the genuine browser build. Evaluate an architecture-neutral WebAssembly path and a CPU-capable low-resource mode; make optional acceleration/threading capability-checked. Do not assume native D3D11/D3D12/Vulkan backends are available inside a browser. Define minimum browser/device tiers, then verify startup, memory, input/audio, asset transfer and full-match play on at least one older x86 system and one ARM Chromebook before claiming support. Report unsupported APIs or insufficient hardware clearly; do not promise every Chromebook will run it.
Current toolchain audit (2026-10-15): no emcc/emcmake/wasm-ld/wasmtime is on PATH, and the searched project build configuration has native TARGET_PC and desktop Dawn/WebGPU wiring but no Emscripten/browser target. This is a missing build prerequisite, not proof of technical impossibility. Add and pin the browser toolchain at the browser milestone after native gameplay acceptance.

LAUNCHER REQUIREMENT CLARIFICATION (2026-10-05)
Bundle two separate launchers/build targets in the same desktop package. The local game EXE provides single-player and native P2P multiplayer lobby hosting/joining. The browser-host launcher starts the browser build and asset server, lets the host configure bind IP/hostname and port, and displays a copyable join URL. Guests open that URL in their own browsers, download authorized assets with per-client progress visible in the lobby, and run the game client in the browser. Track LAN hosting and Internet reachability separately; a configured IP URL alone does not establish remote connectivity. Both launchers must report startup failures clearly. Browser delivery requires an actual browser-compatible game build and separate gameplay/input/audio/network validation, not merely opening the native EXE from a web page. Keep source and rebuild instructions for both bundled targets synchronized.

OVERALL PROJECT PROGRESS REPORTING (2026-10-05)
At every meaningful user-facing project update, include an approximate percentage complete for the ENTIRE requested project. Include native gameplay and all standard content, fidelity/timing/input/audio, no-save flow, both renderers and graphics/audio settings, native mod support, four-player P2P, genuine browser play and authorized asset transfer, both launchers, and synchronized source/rebuild delivery. Do not equate diagnostic builds, clear-frame smoke, or isolated fixtures with playable milestone completion. Base the estimate on documented acceptance milestones, explain material changes in scope or estimates, and distinguish estimates from verified acceptance. Establish and maintain a weighted milestone baseline before reporting the first percentage; never derive progress from elapsed time, token usage, or source line counts. Retain quiet behavior when no meaningful progress or actionable change occurs. This reporting requirement supplements the active goal; it does not change or complete its objective.
Progress baseline: project-completion.json defines full-scope weights and evidence; report-project-completion.py validates weights/ranges and computes the rounded estimate. 2026-10-06 USER MULTIPLAYER MENU DECISION (supersedes earlier menu wording):
Add main-menu button Online. Its submenu has exactly four entries: Host Game, Join Game, LAN Game, Download Play.
Host Game and Join Game use peer-to-peer networking and support the requested four-player lobbies. LAN Game uses local-area-network hosting/joining without requiring an Internet matchmaking service.
Download Play gracefully closes the current native game and hands off to the separately bundled browser-host launcher/build. Start and validate the host service/browser runtime before completing the handoff so a failed launch can be reported coherently. Relaunch genuine game execution in the host's browser and show the host a shareable join URL. Clients join in their browsers with no assets preinstalled; automatically transfer assets the host is authorized to distribute and display each client's download progress in the lobby. Clients still receive the required assets; this is not a claim that original content can be played with no asset data. Preserve separate native single-player/P2P executable and browser-host executable, synchronized modifiable source, and rebuild/mod instructions. LAN URL reachability and public Internet reachability need separate validation; an IP URL alone does not establish access through NAT. Original asset redistribution authorization remains distinct from technical feasibility.
Status: agreed roadmap, implementation/acceptance pending. Whole-project engineering estimate remains approximately21%.

2026-10-06 USER ROADMAP - ONLINE MENU AND DOWNLOAD PLAY
Main menu includes a button titled Online. Its submenu has exactly four options:
Host Game - host a four-player peer-to-peer lobby.
Join Game - join a peer-to-peer lobby.
LAN Game - multiplayer on the local area network.
Download Play - hand off from the native game to the separately bundled browser-host build. Validate that the browser host can start before closing the current native game; relaunch the host's game in a browser and display a shareable host URL. Clients open that URL in their browsers without preinstalled game assets; the host transfers assets it is authorized to distribute automatically. Show each client's asset download progress in the lobby before play. Distinguish LAN-reachable URLs from Internet-reachable hosting and test connectivity. This is true browser execution, not merely video streaming. No claim of implemented or playable Download Play yet.
Acceptance requires all four menu routes, four-player P2P hosting/joining, LAN play, reliable native-to-browser handoff, host browser play, client asset download/progress and browser multiplayer. Existing graphics, audio, native mods, no-save and synchronized-source packaging requirements remain in scope. Estimated overall project completion remains approximately 21%; this roadmap clarification does not increase completion.

The standard particle-bank walker rejects its group-0 second palette/table slot at body offset 1,180 (raw word 0x80a8812a) as out of body bounds. `particle.c` relocates `num*2` pointers when `palnum==0`; therefore this slot's semantics need more source/runtime evidence. No converter exception has been committed for EfKbSs.

Scope remains archive parser support and a bounded muted startup probe, not article/effect model construction, in-match action, general rendering validation, full gameplay, or a playable port. ## Kirby-copy-Samus effect load-path audit — 2026-10-11

## Retail palette word relocation semantics - 2026-10-11

still unresolved; this is not evidence to accept, normalize, or render the

slot before considering a narrow native profile.

## EfKbSs textured palette reachability trace - 2026-10-11

Extended the focused retail audit to inspect the first opcode in command 34000 and cross-check the source branches that enable particle textures and select C8 palettes. The command's first bytes are `40 00`: `particle.c` treats this as texture pose 0, then enables `DispTexture` when texture-table entry 0 is non-null. The in-bank texture offset is 0x40. The command's initial kind does not already have `DispTexture`, so this opcode is the enabling path. `psdisp.c` handles C8 palette selection by indexing the palette table with the particle pose when `palNum` remains 0xFF and `ComTLUT` is clear; the record has `palnum=0`, `palflag=0`, and its palette slot 1 is the out-of-body word at 1180. This establishes a source-reachable path to the suspect palette for the referenced command; it is not a rendered-in-game observation. Consequently the slot cannot be assumed unused, and replacing it with null or an invented texture address would be unsupported. The 32-bit retail bank-add target is still unresolved, so the importer continues to reject this archive safely.

Verification: rebuilt the targeted x86 production-parser harness with `cmd /c work\build-kirby-copy-samus-effect-import.cmd`; the focused `audit-kirby-copy-samus-bank34-live-effect.js` passes the exact profile, texture-opcode/source-path assertions, unchanged-input generic/typed/malformed refusals, failed production parse, and no-allocation-on-refusal checks. The separate palette/DOL audit passes and still reports the runtime target unresolved. These are bounded diagnostics only: the archive is not imported, the effect is not rendered, and the native game remains incomplete. Full project estimate stays 22%; playable-release acceptance is false. The ISO and saves remain untouched; no game was launched.

The command-bytecode path is now decoded more narrowly. For command 34000, a source-shaped decoder consumes 37 bytes through the first wait (`0x04`, wait 4): texture-pose opcode `0x40 0x00`, mirror/rotation setup, prim/env color setup, an eight-count loop mark at offset 22 targeting offset 24, two size commands, then the wait. The loop back/end tail is `0xFB 0xFF`; its loop body consists of those size updates and the wait, with no palette-set opcode. The particle starts with `palNum=0xff`; with this command's `palflag=0` and no initial `ComTLUT`, C8 rendering selects `palettes[poseNum]`. For pose 0 and `num=1`, that is table slot 1, exactly the raw `0x80a8812a` at body offset 1180. This strengthens reachability from table-candidate to a statically decoded source render path, but does not prove a hardware/native frame or reveal a valid target. Do not null or rewrite the value; the native importer remains fail-closed. The harness and archive refusal test still pass as diagnostics only; overall completion estimate remains 22% and playable acceptance remains false.

NATIVE IN-GAME OPTIONS UI REQUIREMENT (added 2026-10-13)
All player-facing presentation, graphics, renderer, and audio settings must be reachable and changeable from the game's own native menu screens (for example, Options > Graphics / Advanced Graphics / Audio). Do not implement these as a small desktop/window overlay button, launcher-only controls, or a separate OS-style panel. The menu design is a first-class in-game screen with controller and keyboard navigation, readable labels, capability-aware choices, safe defaults, and visible confirmation of the active setting. Settings should apply to the running game where feasible and remain session-only unless a separate persistence scope is later approved; they must not depend on memory-card save I/O.

The native Graphics menu roadmap includes: Auto/D3D12/Vulkan selection with capability checks; 16:9, 16:10, 21:9 and automatic display ratio; resolution from 240p through 8K; presentation caps 60/120/240 independently of 60 Hz gameplay simulation; FSR3; shadow enable/resolution; texture quality at full/50%/25%; lighting enable; and an option to force the lowest available fighter LOD. Audio offers Stereo and 5.1 with device capability checks and stereo fallback. Low-end settings must not alter collision or gameplay rules. Acceptance requires opening the actual in-game menu, navigating with supported controls, changing each option, and verifying that the active runtime/backend responds; a window overlay or an API-only smoke test does not meet this requirement.

PRESENTATION-PATH REFINEMENT (2026-10-14)
Further Aurora source inspection clarifies where the correction belongs. `aurora::end_frame()` computes a centered destination rectangle with `webgpu::calculate_present_viewport(surfaceWidth, surfaceHeight, presentSource.width, presentSource.height)` before the final copy. That compositor already preserves the source texture's ratio and centers it on the native surface. The menu distortion is earlier: the original scene draws with a widescreen-sized EFB and GX currently maps logical viewport X/Y with independent scales. Therefore a blit-only change cannot undo stretched pixels. For authored menus/FMV, the source render target and logical GX viewport need to retain their authored ratio, then the existing compositor can letterbox/pillarbox it. The initial FIT runtime-toggle attempt is unsafe during scene startup (see v192/v193); a correct implementation must switch target dimensions only at a VI/XFB-safe scene boundary or use a separately retained authored-aspect render target, and prove stale XFB frames cannot be presented across the switch. Keep widescreen gameplay's source aspect unchanged. This is a narrowed engineering hypothesis from source inspection, not a fix.

RGB-ONLY FRAMEBUFFER ALPHA PIPELINE CORRECTION - 2026-10-17

Status: VERIFIED scoped production renderer fix;overall PARTIALLY VERIFIED.
Project estimate remains approximately27%;goal active. No playable-release acceptance.

The host RGBA attachment always has a backing alpha channel,but GX RGB8/RGB565
framebuffers do not. Pipeline setup previously copied alpha-write and destination-

formats,masks alpha writes unless RGBA6 is selected,and disables destination-alpha

captured pipeline's alpha override. State is normalized BEFORE hashing/caching.
There is no pipeline/shader/command layout change and no user cache deletion.

RGBA6 DESTINATION-ALPHA REPLACEMENT - 2026-10-17

Status: VERIFIED scoped production renderer fix;overall PARTIALLY VERIFIED.
Project estimate remains approximately27%;goal active. No playable-release acceptance.
Supersedes the previous framebuffer-alpha milestone's pending RGBA6 replacement warning.

The old alpha blend equation multiplied source alpha by the requested destination
alpha. A fresh old-binary D3D12 control with the current oracle confirms768incorrect
alpha-probe samples while RGB samples pass. It exits cleanly. The baseline executable,
source snapshots and failed evidence are retained;this is not inferred from source alone.

RGBA6 alpha override now uses paired pipelines for each individual triangle and
instance. The color pass keeps original fragment alpha for RGB blending and leaves
depth/alpha unwritten. The coverage pass keeps original TEV/discard and vertex work,
forces final output alpha to1 AFTER discard,and writes the requested constant alpha
with the original depth test/write. Interleaving each primitive preserves feedback
from earlier overlapping primitives. Index/vertex starts and instance starts remain
those of the real draw. The primary pipeline is restored so the encoder's cached
binding remains coherent. Companion pipelines are published under a mutex and cleared
only after compiler workers join. No DrawData/inline command payload was enlarged.

This compatibility path needs no dual-source blending feature. It adds GPU draws
when an alpha override is active;performance was NOT measured and no FPS gain is
claimed. A capability-checked dual-source fast path remains an optimization option.
The shader's internal force-alpha bit uses reserved space;pipeline config version
advances16->17 for the new semantics. Source uniforms and ordinary game animation
are unchanged. An initial compile error from a missing assertion-log module was
corrected from the compiler output;the failure log is retained.

85/170source alpha with opposite170/85overrides,and overlapping instanced lines.
The strengthened line geometry uses distinct instance ranges,so the probe checks
instance offsets as well as overlap. The earlier order/ suite is retained;accepted
